newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CBA to buy 17 pct of Caspian Group.
newsitem.headline: CBA to buy 17 pct of Caspian Group.

text.p: Commonwealth Bank of Australia said on Wednesday it would buy a 17 percent stake in the Caspian Group, an unlisted emerging markets investment bank.

"The deal will accelerate the bank's Asian strategy by providing additional expertise and distribution for institutional banking products into Asia through Caspian's offices in Hong Kong, Kuala Lumpur and Bangkok," CBA said.
CBA did not say in its statement who it would buy the stake from and did not reveal the purchase price.

The Caspian group was launched in June 1995 by former Baring Securities founder Christopher Heath, employs 260 people and has offices in New York, London, Hong Kong, Mexico, Argentina, Brazil, Bombay, New Delhi, Kuala Lumpur Bangkok and Jakarta.
Caspian is also opening offices in Taipei and Manila.
Rupert Pennant-Rea, former Bank of England deputy governor and editor of The Economist, is Caspian's non-executive chairman.
CBA said the deal would also strengthen its access to investors in the Americas and Europe through Caspian's offices there.
"Whilst the initial focus will be Asia, there is potential to serve clients in emerging markets worldwide," CBA Institutional Banking Head Michael Katz said in a statement.

Caspian Group Chief Executive Christopher Heath said the CBA investment realised Caspian's plan to attract a strong commercial bank as a strategic shareholder whilst retaining the group's independence and partnership structure.
"This investment by the Commonwealth Bank will enable us to enlarge our trading capability, by giving us access to a broader product range for our customers," Heath said in the CBA statement.
Spokesmen for CBA and Caspian were not immediately available to comment on how much was paid for the stake.

CBA's shareholding partners in Caspian include Korea's Ssangyong Investment and Securities, Thailand's National Finance and Securities, Mexican brokerage Vector Casa de Bolsa and Singapore's Philip Securities.
